title: Applying file sync changes from a leased work queue
name: Sync change applier

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this consumer acknowledges, releases, or dead-letters changes? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: The lease is acked at the top of the try block, before the change is applied. If the blob is not uploaded yet, or the index write fails, or the process crashes, the message is already gone from the queue. The later release() or deadLetter() calls act on a lease that was already acked, so the change is never retried and the file silently never syncs. The ack belongs after the index write succeeds.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A change with revision 7 arrives for a path whose index entry is already at revision 9. What does applyOne do?
choices: Overwrites the index entry with revision 7
Releases the message so it is retried later
Acks it and makes no change to the index
choiceQuestions.explanation: The guard current.revision >= change.revision is true (9 >= 7), so the message is acked and the method returns without touching the index. This makes stale or duplicate deliveries harmless. It never overwrites with an older revision and does not treat this as a conflict to retry or dead-letter.

choiceQuestions.prompt: How many changes can the applier work on at the same time, and when does it pull more?
choices: Unlimited; it pulls again as soon as each change is handed off
Up to parallelism (8); it pulls the next batch only after every change in the current batch has settled
Exactly one at a time, in queue order
choiceQuestions.explanation: pull(this.parallelism) fetches up to 8 envelopes, and run() awaits Promise.allSettled over them before pulling again. allSettled also means one rejected applyOne does not cut the wait short. Nothing groups by workspace, and changes in a batch run concurrently, not one by one.

choiceQuestions.prompt: Two changes for the same path, revisions 3 and 4, land in the same batch and the index is at revision 2. What ordering guarantee does the code provide?
choices: Revision 4 always wins because the batch is sorted by revision
Revision 3 always wins because it was enqueued first
The queue guarantees per-path FIFO, so they are applied in order
None within a batch: both read revision 2, both pass the guard, and whichever upsert finishes last wins
choiceQuestions.explanation: Both applyOne calls run concurrently and read the index before either writes, so both see revision 2 and pass the guard. The final index state depends on which upsert lands last. Nothing sorts the batch or uses the queue for per-path ordering, and the upsert is not conditional on revision.
